# The three-valued X = Y of intervals, two-limb bounds

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/*/brute/, results/brute-code.json and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `interval_equal_2` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

The three-valued answer to whether $x = y$ for every $x \in X, y \in Y$, $X$ and $Y$ not being empty, $X = [x_l, x_u]$ and $Y = [y_l, y_u]$: *yes* only if it holds for every choice of members, *no* only if it fails for every choice, otherwise *unknown*, both masks false:

$$\mathit{yes} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y, \qquad \mathit{no} \implies X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x = y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y.$$

A number of several limbs stands for their exact sum: $x_l = x_{l0} + x_{l1}$, $x_u = x_{u0} + x_{u1}$, $y_l = y_{l0} + y_{l1}$, $y_u = y_{u0} + y_{u1}$.

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `equal(X, Y)` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Trit` | `constexpr`; does not round |
| `not_equal(X, Y)` | `Interval<T, 2>`, `Interval<T, 2>` | `Trit` | the answer of `equal(X, Y)` with yes and no exchanged; `constexpr`; does not round |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $X = [x_l, x_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $x_l = +\infty$ and $x_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $x_l \le x_u$, $x_l < +\infty$, $x_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.
- $Y = [y_l, y_u]$ is a canonical interval: the empty set, $y_l = +\infty$ and $y_u = -\infty$ (each followed by a zero), or a nonempty interval, neither bound a NaN, $y_l \le y_u$, $y_l < +\infty$, $y_u > -\infty$, each bound finite and normalized or $(\pm\infty, \pm 0)$; its members are the real numbers between its bounds.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- $\mathit{yes}$ is true only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; $\mathit{no}$ only if $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x = y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; never both. Both false is the answer *unknown*.
- An empty operand gives *unknown*, and so does the whole line.
- Exact: $\mathit{yes}$ is true exactly when $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } x = y \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$, and $\mathit{no}$ exactly when $X \ne \emptyset, Y \ne \emptyset \text{ and } \lnot(x = y) \text{ for every } x \in X, y \in Y$; *unknown* is returned exactly when neither holds.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 1 bit, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `interval_equal_2_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeIntervalPredicates.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions interval_equal_2_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `interval_equal_2_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** the bounds compared, and a test of emptiness (Milestone 2 listing). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/interval_equal_2.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/interval_equal_2.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`eq_2_2`](eq_2_2.md), [`lt_2_2`](lt_2_2.md).

```
# The three-valued X = Y of intervals with 2-limb bounds (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface",
# "Comparisons"): yes when every member of X equals every member of Y, that is X = Y = [v, v], x_l =
# x_u = y_l = y_u; no when no member of X equals one of Y, the intervals disjoint, x_u < y_l or y_u
# < x_l; both false otherwise and when an operand is empty (the yes of the empty set fails by
# itself: its bounds differ). By the comparisons of two limbs, exact on canonical values, and the
# leading limbs for the test of emptiness. Exact. For every precision.

ea  = eq_2_2(xl0, xl1, xu0, xu1)
eb  = eq_2_2(xu0, xu1, yl0, yl1)
ec  = eq_2_2(yl0, yl1, yu0, yu1)
eab = and(ea, eb)
yes = and(eab, ec)
nx  = lt(xl0, const inf)
ny  = lt(yl0, const inf)
ne  = and(nx, ny)
da  = lt_2_2(xu0, xu1, yl0, yl1)
db  = lt_2_2(yu0, yu1, xl0, xl1)
dd  = or(da, db)
no  = and(dd, ne)
```

## Measured

The stored brute-force runs of this kernel's code: the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound. A run is shown only if it ran the code the kernel has now: its generated C++ (scalar and packed, every kernel it calls inlined, with the functions it calls; comments left out) must be the same at the commit of the run, as the fingerprints in [`results/brute-code.json`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/results/brute-code.json) show ([How to read a page](reading.md#what-the-measured-numbers-are)).

**Milestone 2**: the runs of commit `5f597fb`, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#interval_equal_2)).
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 7 200 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 9 316 599 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
